segments.text: > Part of the [Implementation Status](README.md) index. Node-`fs`-shaped synchronous file I/O for reading/writing config, data, and logs — not `File`/`FileReader`/`FileSystemFileHandle` (those model browser sandbox/permission concepts that don't exist for a native CLI/microservice program with direct filesystem access).

caveats: Text-only by design — a file with embedded null bytes reads back shorter than its real size (`.length` is `strlen`-based); use `fs.readFileSyncBytes(path)` for a binary file
notes: Reads the whole file into a string
Throws a catchable `Error` (built from `strerror(errno)`) if the file can't be opened
See [ADR-00023](../adr/ADR-00023.md)
Binary-safe sibling of `readFileSync`: returns a `Uint8Array` with the file's exact byte count (no `strlen` involved), so a file with an embedded null byte reads back whole
No `Buffer` class — this compiler has none; plain `ArrayBuffer`/TypedArrays instead
See [ADR-00094](../adr/ADR-00094.md)
caveats: `err.code` matches Node (`e.code === 'ENOENT'`/`'EEXIST'`/… — [ADR-00684](../adr/ADR-00684.md)); the numeric `err.errno`, `err.path`, and `err.syscall` remain absent, and the message text differs from Node's `ENOENT: …, <syscall> '<path>'` format.

notes: Creates or truncates the file with `data`. Throws on failure

`data` may be a string (the original, `strlen`-based path, unchanged) or an `ArrayBuffer`/TypedArray (binary-safe, writes the real byte count via `fwrite` directly — [ADR-00094](../adr/ADR-00094.md)), dispatched on `data`'s inferred type
caveats: `err.code` matches Node (`e.code === 'ENOENT'`/`'EEXIST'`/… — [ADR-00684](../adr/ADR-00684.md)); the numeric `err.errno`, `err.path`, and `err.syscall` remain absent, and the message text differs from Node's `ENOENT: …, <syscall> '<path>'` format.
No third `options` argument — `writeFileSync(p, d, 'utf8')` / `{ flag: 'a' }` are compile errors (`encoding`/`mode`/`flag` unavailable — use `appendFileSync` to append).

notes: Like `writeFileSync`, but appends instead of truncating (creates the file if it doesn't exist). Throws on failure
Same string/`ArrayBuffer`/TypedArray dispatch as `writeFileSync`
caveats: `err.code` matches Node (`e.code === 'ENOENT'`/`'EEXIST'`/… — [ADR-00684](../adr/ADR-00684.md)); the numeric `err.errno`, `err.path`, and `err.syscall` remain absent, and the message text differs from Node's `ENOENT: …, <syscall> '<path>'` format.
No third `options` argument (`encoding`/`mode`/`flag` rejected at compile time).

notes: Plain existence check via POSIX `access()`
Deliberately does **not** throw for a missing path — matches real Node's own `existsSync`, one of the few `fs` functions that reports "doesn't exist" as `false` rather than an error

caveats: The full numeric Stats surface is exposed — `dev`/`mode`/`nlink`/`uid`/`gid`/`rdev`/`blksize`/`ino`/`size`/`blocks`/`atimeMs`/`mtimeMs`/`ctimeMs`/`birthtimeMs` plus `isFile()`/`isDirectory()`/`isSymbolicLink()` ([ADR-00565](../adr/ADR-00565.md)) — but not the Date-valued `atime`/`mtime`/`ctime`/`birthtime` accessors; times are integer milliseconds only ([ADR-00495](../adr/ADR-00495.md)/[ADR-00497](../adr/ADR-00497.md))
`birthtimeMs` is `0` on Linux — glibc's `struct stat` carries no creation time (it needs `statx`); Darwin reports the real `st_birthtimespec`
`rmSync` options must be a `{recursive, force}` boolean-literal object; no `maxRetries`/`retryDelay`
`readlinkSync` caps targets at 4096 bytes; `accessSync`'s mode defaults to existence-only (F_OK) with no `fs.constants` to name others ([ADR-00497](../adr/ADR-00497.md))
`openSync` flags must be a string literal (`r r+ w w+ a a+ wx ax`) or a raw numeric mask — no `fs.constants` names
`writeSync` writes string data only (no Buffer/offset/length variant); `readSync`'s buffer must be a `Uint8Array`/`Buffer` ([ADR-00498](../adr/ADR-00498.md))

notes: Deletes a file. Throws on failure
caveats: `err.code` matches Node (`e.code === 'ENOENT'`/`'EEXIST'`/… — [ADR-00684](../adr/ADR-00684.md)); the numeric `err.errno`, `err.path`, and `err.syscall` remain absent, and the message text differs from Node's `ENOENT: …, <syscall> '<path>'` format.
Options support only the literal `{ recursive: true }` (creates every missing prefix, idempotent — [ADR-00487](../adr/ADR-00487.md)); the plain form still throws on an existing path or missing parent
notes: Creates a directory via POSIX `mkdir()`, mode `0777` reduced by the process umask as usual
See [ADR-00027](../adr/ADR-00027.md)
Removes an *empty* directory via POSIX `rmdir()` — deliberately directory-only (fails on a plain file, unlike `remove()`/`unlinkSync`)

`{ recursive: true }` removes the whole tree by routing to `rmSync`'s recursive removal ([ADR-00578](../adr/ADR-00578.md)); Node deprecated the option on `rmdirSync` in favor of `rmSync` but still honors it, and a missing path still throws (no `force`)
See [ADR-00027](../adr/ADR-00027.md)
Lists a directory's entries (excluding `.`/`..`) as a `string[]`, in whatever order the OS's own `readdir()` returns them — no ordering guarantee, matching real Node

Built from `struct dirent`'s `d_name` field at a `runtime.GOOS`-conditional byte offset, independently verified by a compiled `offsetof` probe on both Darwin and (via Docker, see [ADR-00051](../adr/ADR-00051.md)) x86-64 Linux
See [ADR-00027](../adr/ADR-00027.md)
caveats: `err.code` matches Node (`e.code === 'ENOENT'`/`'EEXIST'`/… — [ADR-00684](../adr/ADR-00684.md)); the numeric `err.errno`, `err.path`, and `err.syscall` remain absent, and the message text differs from Node's `ENOENT: …, <syscall> '<path>'` format.
Path only — no `options`; `withFileTypes` (a `Dirent[]`), `recursive`, and `encoding: 'buffer'` are unsupported (always a one-level `string[]`).

notes: Renames/moves a file via POSIX `rename()`. Throws on failure
See [ADR-00027](../adr/ADR-00027.md)
caveats: `err.code` matches Node (`e.code === 'ENOENT'`/`'EEXIST'`/… — [ADR-00684](../adr/ADR-00684.md)); the numeric `err.errno`, `err.path`, and `err.syscall` remain absent, and the message text differs from Node's `ENOENT: …, <syscall> '<path>'` format.

`err.code` matches Node (`e.code === 'ENOENT'`/`'EEXIST'`/… — [ADR-00684](../adr/ADR-00684.md)); the numeric `err.errno`, `err.path`, and `err.syscall` remain absent, and the message text differs from Node's `ENOENT: …, <syscall> '<path>'` format.
No `mode` argument — `fs.constants.COPYFILE_EXCL`/`FICLONE` unsupported; always overwrites the destination.
notes: Binary-safe: composes the raw `__kml_fs_read_file_raw`/`__kml_fs_write_file_bytes` helpers ([ADR-00094](../adr/ADR-00094.md)), threading the source's exact byte count, so a file with an embedded null byte copies back whole — no new C-level I/O code

rows.feature: Async variants — callback (`fs.readFile(path, cb)`) + Promise (`fs.promises.readFile` / `import from 'fs/promises'`)
caveats: Blocking I/O under the hood — this compiler has no thread pool, so the syscall runs inline; only *delivery* is async (the callback fires right after the op, the Promise is returned already settled). Not a concurrency/performance gain, an API-shape one ([TDD-00107](../tdd/TDD-00107.md)/[ADR-00340](../adr/ADR-00340.md))
`readFile` delivers a string (text) — inherits `readFileSync`'s text-only caveat; no async binary (`Buffer`) form
No `options`/`encoding` argument; no async `stat` (no sync `stat` exists either)
notes: Covers the sync set: `readFile`/`writeFile`/`appendFile`/`unlink`/`mkdir`/`rmdir`/`rename`/`copyFile`/`readdir`. Callback gets `(err[, data])`; the Promise rejects with the same `Error` the sync form throws
Reuses each `*Sync` runtime helper verbatim, catching its throw via the compiler's own `setjmp` catch primitive — no parallel non-throwing I/O code

caveats: Chunks are **strings**, not `Buffer`s — text-first, like `readFileSync` (an embedded NUL truncates a chunk); binary (`Uint8Array`) streaming is a follow-on
`createReadStream` reads eagerly to EOF at construction (chunked, not a lazy pull) — a huge file is fully read into per-chunk buffers
Options: `createReadStream` takes `{ highWaterMark }`, `createWriteStream` `{ flags: "w"\|"a" }` — both compile-time literals; `start`/`end`/`fd`/`encoding` are clean errors
notes: `createReadStream` returns a Node `Readable` (consumable via `for await` or `.on('data')`/`.on('end')`/`.pipe()`); `createWriteStream` a Node `Writable` (`.write`/`.end`, `'finish'`/`'close'`/`'drain'`). A read→write `.pipe()` round-trips. A failed open throws a catchable `Error` (like `readFileSync`) ([TDD-00108](../tdd/TDD-00108.md)/[ADR-00343](../adr/ADR-00343.md))
Also wired `for await` over any Node `Readable` (was WHATWG-only)

**Differentiator (scoped — [TDD-00172](../tdd/TDD-00172.md)).** Splits in two: the **data layer** (`File extends Blob`, `FileReader.readAsText`/`ArrayBuffer`/`DataURL`) is a thin fs-backed reinterpretation with no UI — path-backed `File`s, reads firing `onload` on the event loop; the **picker layer** (`showOpenFilePicker` → `FileSystemFileHandle`) resolves a path through a pluggable UI backend — a `klain:tui` file-picker widget, a `klain:webview` native dialog, or an explicit-path degradation when headless. Serves interactive native apps (TUI file managers/editors); the data layer is the near-term, standalone-useful piece.
